title: Lonely Deaths Lie Thick as Snow
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Police detective Jin Saeki answers a burglary call at an empty mansion and finds the bodies of 13 children, starved, and a strange symbol; a manhunt begins for the owner, Juzo Haikawa (Kodansha blurb; ANN). Juzo's daughter Kanon says he took in abused and neglected children, one of them Jin's younger half-brother, and the surviving children insist Juzo did not do it (ANN). The case reopens Jin's own childhood abuse (ANN). Seinen crime drama, rated T+ in English (ANN).
life_message: Children failed by their own families deserve to be seen and protected, and chosen family can stand in where blood family betrayed them.

content.note: Dead and starved children, a DVD of their last moments, child abuse and domestic violence (ANN content warning; MU Blood and Gore, Cannibalism, Murder/s).
ANN reviewers call it 'intense' and 'disturbing', 'not... for you' if squeamish; art 'mostly keeps things at a distance'.
AniList tags Nudity; MU lists subtle romance; context not described (to verify).
Adult police drama; not described in sources (to verify).
Jin's traumatic childhood abuse resurfaces (ANN); MU Traumatic Past, Abuse, Starvation.
Crimes against children are the mystery, not models; Jin is described as 'cocky' (blurb).

dominant: Justice for abused children; found family versus failed birth family; the past's grip on the present

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Police process pursues the case; MU also lists Revenge, so personal score-settling may enter (to verify).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Police detective protagonist and a formal manhunt (blurb; ANN).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Jin's half-brother among the children; found family theme (ANN).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Police ranks present; MU Secret Organization/s and Clan/s; not central in summaries.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Starvation, abandonment and survival of abused children (MU; ANN).

folkways.japan: The story sits in a Japanese police procedural setting where family shame and keeping abuse hidden inside the household are part of what the investigation must break through.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewers describe found-family and 'invisible crimes' themes carried by the mystery; neither calls it preachy.
delivery.note: The theme of abused children's suffering is carried by the investigation rather than by speeches, as far as the sources show.

winners_losers: Sympathy lies with the abused children and with Jin as he faces his past; abusive and neglectful parents are the moral losers, while Juzo's guilt is left open in the early volumes.
